_about: v16.1 patch, made in the main tree after the v16 gate (notes/gate-v16-r1) and the v16 verifier (notes/workflows/review-v16-verify.json). Evidence: notes/v16-patch1-evidence/. Not run in this patch: the quality suite, the full perf suite, the GLSL pages, the tour audit, the Russian walk, the sound recordings at 48 kHz, the real Android phone. The machine had another job running (load 14 to 22) and free disk fell from 10 GB to 2.8 GB from outside this work.

items.note: Cause: the globe drew a forward stand-in for one frame while the inverse program compiled; its map-cache texture (4096 x 37 RG32F, 1.2 MB) stayed. In v15.2.1 a mesh rebuild 0.4 s after the load freed it by chance; v16 keeps its first mesh (the saved clipWin), so the texture stayed. Fix: app.js notes the stand-in's cache keys (noteStandIn) and frees them when that shape first draws inverse (notePath -> dropStandIn -> GLR.dropCached, new in gl.js). Paired perf re-run: gpu_live_bytes 2.59 MiB -> 1.43 MiB (limit 2.55), gpu_live_end_bytes 920.8 KiB (v15.2.1: 920.8 KiB). The rest is the step thumbnails' scratch textures, freed by design about 1.5 s later.

Paired re-run: 196, 213 and 208 ms (limit 264), no slow rep (v16 had 5 of 12 slow). The slow mode (about 320 ms) predates v16 (v15.2.1: 1 of 15). Its cause was not traced in this time box. The same run failed other example timings (compile_ms, first_frame_ms, settle_ms of examples 2, 7, 8, 13) at load 17 on 10 cores; the runner warns to re-run them. They were not judged here. None of this patch's changes touches shader compiles. Re-run the examples unit at the gate on a quiet machine.

Cause: the far tail of a long line under the map. Its samples grow geometrically; the GPU draws each segment as 8 straight pieces, so a tail step of up to 1.8 rad of the circle drew a chord about 1 px inside it. v15.2.1 had the same chords (worst 0.95 px); v16's meshing window comes from the view, so the chords fell elsewhere and one ink pixel landed 2.68 px away. Fix (region.js Lines.refine): resolveFar halves a far segment until its image midpoint is within 1/32 of its chord (worst chord 0.95 px -> 0.018 px at 150 px per unit); wrapCut ends a tail once the image turned 2.5 pi beyond expandBox(win, 4), the run stop's own rule. exp of a vertical line: 1059 -> 939 segments. t_lines passes (its cost bound too). curves_cmd: pass, exp_imag_axis max 2.32 px, 0 far pixels (evidence/curves.json).

items.status: rejected with evidence (test window); no app change
items.note: The detection is not a harp pluck. Every counted click is 6.0 to 6.9 ms after the start of the scrub's landmark (the wooden note at t = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1). Its knock and its 9 kHz partial peak 4.2 to 10 ms after the start in every landmark, 13 to 31 dB over the background. The test logs every cue with the strings' 6 ms window, so a landmark whose peak falls after 6 ms is counted. v15.2.1 does the same: 2 clicks in 12 scrub files, both 6.0 to 6.1 ms after a landmark (v16: 2 in 16, 6.1 and 6.9 ms). Proposal for the user (a change to the test, so not made): log non-string cues with the detector's own 150 ms window, as test/sound_clicks.py documents.

Cause: v16 updates the transport every frame in Phase and Landscape too (review sound-picture-2). On a phone each update was a full style recalc of about 1.6 to 2 ms, caused by one CSS rule, .fader-stops:has(> button[style*="--at"]): a style attribute inside :has() makes every inline style change a broad recalc (the scrubber's --fill every frame). Nothing sets --at, so the rule is removed (page.html). Also: the readout's Text node is updated, not replaced; while playing the scrubber moves in half-pixel steps (exact when paused); syncTransport reads the scrubber width before it writes. Phone metrics, 3 s of play: style recalc 305-367 ms -> 22-29 ms; task time 551-624 ms -> 284-382 ms (v15.2.1: 170 to 550). Paired with v15.2.1 (load 14): 390 px Phase 17.4-17.8 vs 17.5, Landscape 17.6-17.8 vs 17.5-17.6, 1440 px within 0.7 ms. One first rep at 390 px X -> Y read 18.7 ms (its other reps 17.6-17.8; v15.2.1 17.7-17.8): not a regression by the paired rule.
